page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 virtual CPUs, which map to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. A key characteristic of this instance is its bundled local storage, consisting of a 1919 GB SSD. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and virtualization is managed via the KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.i2.2xlarge exhibits lower-tier processing and memory performance. Single-core and multi-core CPU benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, consistently fall into the bottom 25% of tested servers. Memory read bandwidth is also limited, with small-block cached reads at 328.53 GB/sec and large-block uncached reads at 39.23 GB/sec placing in the weak category. However, memory write bandwidth for large blocks shows average performance at 35.45 GB/sec. Cryptographic and database operations, including Redis SET performance at 6.06 million operations per second, also rank in the bottom 25%.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.i2.2xlarge is the combination of high-capacity local SSD storage and moderate memory density against relatively weak CPU compute capabilities. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance is optimized for workloads that require significant local storage capacity and memory space rather than raw processing power. Appropriate workloads include local database hosting, caching layers, and storage-intensive applications that can operate within the 2 Gbps baseline network limit and do not demand high-frequency CPU performance.
